name: Predictive Assist
description: Bot-assisted play: clicks for you right before a death, holds back clicks that would kill you when waiting a step or two survives, and replays early clicks on landings and orbs.

sec-general.name: General
sec-general.description:
This mod changes your inputs. Runs made with it are bot-assisted and not valid for leaderboards or demon lists.

Timings are in **physics steps**. At the default 240 TPS, 1 step is about 4 ms and 4 steps is about one frame at 60 FPS. If you use a TPS bypass, the numbers are steps at your TPS.

show-label.name: Show 'Bot-assisted' label
show-label.description: Shows a label in the top-left corner with how many inputs were delayed or buffered this attempt.

sec-learn.name: Learn from my attempts
sec-learn.description: Uses your recorded attempts on this level. Where your clicks have worked before, early clicks are held back to that spot and, if you have not clicked by the end of it, the mod clicks for you. Cube, ball, robot and spider. Needs Record attempts on to keep learning.

learn-early.name: Learned: early window (steps)
learn-early.description: How early a click before a learned spot is held back instead of going through. 12 steps is about 50 ms at 240 TPS.

learn-block.name: Learned: block bad clicks
learn-block.description: Drops a click at a spot where clicking has killed you every time (at least 3 times) and getting past without clicking there has worked (at least 3 times).

sec-save.name: Auto-click save
sec-save.description: When you are about to die and a click right now would survive, the mod clicks for you. This is the part that helps when you click too late. It only steps in while you are not holding the button, and only if the simulation can see the death coming (it stops at orbs, pads and most portals).

save-window.name: Save window (steps)
save-window.description: How close to a death the mod may click for you. Bigger is stronger. 10 steps is about 40 ms at 240 TPS; 40 steps is about 170 ms, which will play most simple jumps for you.

save-hold.name: Auto-click length (steps)
save-hold.description: How long the auto-click holds the button. Short is a tap; longer gives higher robot jumps and longer ship/UFO/swing climbs.

plan-ahead.name: Plan ahead: cube, ball, robot, spider (steps)
plan-ahead.description: Before an auto-click, the mod checks this far ahead that the jump leaves a way through, allowing for the next couple of jumps. It skips jumps that land you in a dead end and waits for a better one. 240 steps is about one second at 240 TPS. 0 turns it off.

sec-predict.name: Predictive delay
sec-predict.description:
When you click or release, the mod simulates what happens. If doing it now kills you but waiting a few steps does not, the input waits for the first safe step.

The simulation stops at orbs, pads and most portals and lets those inputs through unchanged. The early-click buffer below covers orbs.

max-delay.name: Max delay (steps)
max-delay.description: How long an input may be held back. 5 steps is about 20 ms at 240 TPS.

lookahead-ground.name: Look-ahead: cube, ball, robot, spider (steps)
lookahead-ground.description: How far past the input the simulation checks for a death. Longer catches more but trusts the simulation further ahead.

lookahead-fly.name: Look-ahead: ship, UFO, wave, swing (steps)
lookahead-fly.description: Shorter than ground modes because the simulation assumes you hold or release for the whole look-ahead, which is rarely true in fly modes.

assist-releases.name: Also delay releases
assist-releases.description: Matters for ship, wave and robot, where letting go is an input.

sec-early.name: Early-click buffer
sec-early.description: Cube, ball, robot and spider. A tap in the air that you release before landing is replayed when you touch the ground or an orb within the window, with the same tap length (so robot jumps keep their height).

early-window.name: Early window (steps)
early-window.description: How early a tap can be and still count. Larger windows can fire a tap meant for an orb on a landing that comes first.

sec-debug.name: Testing
sec-debug.description: Use these to check that the simulation matches the real game.

show-path.name: Show predicted path
show-path.description: Draws the simulated path for the last assisted input: green when the chosen timing survives, red when nothing survived. If the green path does not match where you actually go, the simulation is wrong in that spot.

record.name: Record attempts
record.description: Writes every click, assist action and death to attempts.csv in the mod's save folder, with a guess at why the assist did not save you. Use it to see where and why you die.

debug.name: Debug logging
debug.description: Logs every auto-click, delayed and buffered input to the Geode console.
